title: The Minimal Phenomenal Experience questionnaire (MPE-92M): Towards a phenomenological profile of 'pure awareness' experiences in meditators

cost.compute_notes: All analyses on CPU. validate_synthetic.py 99s; run_replicability.py 250s (14 values of k x 30 split-halves x 2 EFA fits, plus permutation null); run_clone_test.py ~150s; run_clone_oblique.py ~180s; run_perturbation_sweep.py ~90s. Single EFA fit (92 items, n~700) ~0.2s. Total compute under 15 min wall clock. 2026-08-21 addendum: run_self_factor_stability.py, 3 versions (leakage bug, null bug, corrected), each under 30s; total added compute under 2 min.

claims.statement: The authors report a 12-factor solution for the 92-item MPE-92M, explaining 44% of variance, selected on 'joint conceptual and statistical considerations'.
claims.scope: N=1403 self-selected meditators reporting 'pure awareness' experiences, 5 languages, online survey Jan-Mar 2020.

quantities.name: n_factors_reported
quantities.baseline: authors' own EFA, Spearman/principal/quartimin, joint conceptual+statistical criterion

quantities.name: analysis_sample_size
quantities.baseline: filter over85items==1 applied to 3627 submissions

our_assessment.why: The sample filter and N reproduce exactly from the released .dta. The 12 is accepted as an accurate description of what the authors chose, not as an estimate of a number of dimensions in the phenomenon -- see c2 and c3. The authors' own wording ('joint conceptual and statistical considerations') already concedes that the 12th factor is a conceptual addition.

claims.statement: The number of extractable factors is a resolution choice, not a property of the data: three defensible decision rules give 11, 12 and 18 on the same correlation matrix.
claims.scope: Our reanalysis of the released raw data, not a claim the authors make.

quantities.baseline: Horn parallel analysis, 50 column-permuted datasets, Spearman, both mean and 95th-pct thresholds

quantities.baseline: Spearman eigenvalues, cumulative

our_assessment.why: Computed first-hand from the released data; the three rules are all standard and all applied to the identical matrix.

claims.statement: At the resolution of a half-sample, the MPE-92M contains no discretely identifiable factors at any k. Split-half Tucker congruence decays smoothly with no cliff, and at every k >= 5 zero factors reach the .95 'factors are equal' criterion, while every factor at every k exceeds a column-permutation null. This is the claim that qualifies c2: the count is not merely under-determined by the choice of rule.
claims.scope: N=1403, 92 items, 30 random half-splits per k, k in 2..18. Paper's own EFA settings.

quantities.name: split_half_congruence_max
quantities.baseline: k=5, strongest factor, median matched Tucker phi over 30 half-splits (n=701 each)

quantities.name: n_factors_above_congruence_95
quantities.baseline: any k >= 5, median matched Tucker phi over 30 half-splits

quantities.name: n_factors_above_congruence_85
quantities.baseline: k=12, median matched Tucker phi over 30 half-splits

quantities.name: mean_split_half_congruence
quantities.baseline: k=12, real data, mean over 12 matched factors of median phi; 15 half-splits, seed 777 (sweep run)

quantities.name: congruence_permutation_null_max
quantities.baseline: k=18, column-permuted real data preserving item marginals, median matched phi of strongest factor

our_assessment.why: The instrument was validated before use on three synthetic cases with known answers: it recovers exactly 5 of 12 requested factors at phi=.99 with a cliff to .76 when 5 true factors exist; it returns .10-.33 and never approaches .85 on pure noise at every k tested; and it does not inflate spurious factors in a general-plus-specific structure. So the smooth real profile is not an artifact of the estimator.

claims.statement: The non-replicability is misspecification, not estimation noise. A parametric-bootstrap clone generated from the model's OWN fitted loadings and uniquenesses, at the same N and k, is far more replicable than the data it was fitted to -- a stable deficit of +0.13 to +0.14 mean Tucker phi across k = 5, 8, 12. Building the clone with the estimated oblique factor correlations does not close the gap; at k=5 it widens it.
claims.scope: Same data. Clone factor scores normal, uniquenesses inherited from the fit.

quantities.name: mean_split_half_congruence
quantities.baseline: k=12, real data, same statistic; 20 half-splits, seed 312 (clone run) -- differs from the 0.758 row only by split count and seed, which brackets the Monte Carlo error at ~0.01

quantities.name: mean_split_half_congruence
quantities.baseline: k=12, orthogonal parametric-bootstrap clone of the fitted 12-factor model

quantities.name: clone_congruence_deficit
quantities.baseline: k=12, clone mean minus real mean matched phi

quantities.name: clone_congruence_deficit
quantities.baseline: k=5, orthogonal clone mean minus real mean matched phi

quantities.name: clone_congruence_deficit
quantities.baseline: k=5, OBLIQUE clone (factors ~ N(0, Phi_hat)) mean minus real mean matched phi

quantities.name: mean_abs_loading
quantities.baseline: k=12 oblimin solution on full sample

our_assessment.why: This is the test designed to kill c3 and it failed to. The weak-loadings/low-power explanation predicts clone ~= real; observed gap is stable at +0.13-0.14 across three values of k. The obliquity confound was tested explicitly because it was the most plausible remaining rescue, and it runs the wrong way.

claims.statement: The covariance structure of pure-awareness reports is not detectably shaped by meditation tradition, questionnaire language, sex, Buddhist identification or psychedelic use. Across 8 groupings x 2 values of k, between-group factor congruence tracks a size-matched permutation null; only language at k=12 falls below it (p=.040, uncorrected for 16 comparisons) and Zen and metta at k=5 sit above their nulls.
claims.scope: N=1403. Traditions are non-exclusive in this questionnaire, so each is tested as practises-X vs does-not.

quantities.name: between_group_congruence_p_value
quantities.baseline: questionnaire language group 3 (n=889) vs group 1 (n=440), k=12, one-sided empirical p vs 25 size-matched random splits of the pooled sample

quantities.name: between_group_congruence_p_value
quantities.baseline: sex, k=12, same test

quantities.name: between_group_congruence_p_value
quantities.baseline: Vipassana practitioners vs not, k=12, same test

quantities.name: between_group_congruence_p_value
quantities.baseline: Zen practitioners vs not, k=12, same test

quantities.name: between_group_congruence_p_value
quantities.baseline: psychedelic users vs not, k=12, same test

quantities.name: n_groupings_below_size_matched_null
quantities.baseline: 8 grouping variables x k in {5,12}, threshold p<.05 uncorrected

our_assessment.why: A negative result, and the design bounds it in the safe direction: non-exclusive tradition membership makes each contrast weaker than a pure between-tradition one, biasing toward finding no difference. So it supports 'no large tradition effect on covariance structure' and cannot support 'no effect at all'. The size-matched null is what makes it interpretable -- raw between-group congruence would confound group difference with group size.

claims.statement: RECORDED AS NOT-IDENTIFIABLE, against my own analysis. A two-subpopulation loading perturbation of c = 2.0 x mean|loading| reproduces the observed congruence deficit to three decimals (.757 vs .758) -- but the relationship is non-monotonic (c = 3.0 returns to .837), so c is not identified by this statistic and must not be quoted as an estimate of latent heterogeneity.
claims.scope: k=12, 15 half-splits per sweep point, c in {0, .6, 1, 1.5, 2, 3}.

quantities.name: heterogeneity_calibration_c
quantities.baseline: k=12, two-subpopulation loading perturbation matching real mean phi -- NON-IDENTIFIED, see status

quantities.name: mean_split_half_congruence
quantities.baseline: k=12, c=0 (homogeneous clone), sweep control

quantities.name: mean_split_half_congruence
quantities.baseline: k=12, c=3.0 -- ABOVE the c=2.0 value, demonstrating non-monotonicity

our_assessment.why: Two values of c produce the same mean phi, so the statistic does not determine c. Recorded rather than deleted because a three-decimal match is exactly the kind of too-clean agreement that gets quoted as a finding. The only defensible reading is directional: matching the deficit by two-group heterogeneity would require between-group loading differences about twice the mean loading itself, which is not credible and therefore argues against the mixture explanation rather than for it.

claims.statement: CORRECTS an earlier, uncomputed claim in NOTES.md ('the self/subject-object factor is consistently among the top-ranked and most stable'). Properly computed with independent split-halves (self-factor identified within each half separately, no full-sample leakage), the self/subject-object factor has ORDINARY split-half stability -- median rank 3rd of 5 factors at k=5, 5th of 7 at k=7, phi statistically close to the population median-of-medians -- not exceptional stability. It IS real: median phi 0.76-0.80 decisively clears a correctly-implemented permutation null (median 0.14, max 0.36).
claims.scope: Same N=1403, same k=5/k=7 EFA solutions as c3-c6. 30 independent split-halves for the rank/phi computation, 15 for the permutation null (per-column numpy shuffle of one half, which destroys covariance while preserving item marginals).

quantities.name: self_factor_split_half_phi
quantities.baseline: k=7, median over 30 independent split-halves, self-factor identified within each half by mean |loading| on 6 self/boundary items

quantities.name: self_factor_rank_among_k_factors
quantities.baseline: k=7, median rank where 1=most stable of 7 matched factors

quantities.name: population_median_of_medians_phi
quantities.baseline: k=7, all factors, for comparison against the self-factor's 0.801 -- indistinguishable from average

quantities.name: self_factor_permutation_null_max
quantities.baseline: k=7, 15 splits, per-column-shuffled half B, self-factor's own matched phi against the shuffled data

our_assessment.why: A first attempt at both the stability check and its permutation-null control had bugs that each produced a flattering-then-alarming wrong answer in sequence: (1) matching each half against the FULL sample (which partly contains that half) gave an inflated phi (0.92-0.95) and a rank that looked exceptional -- data leakage; (2) the first permutation null used pandas `.apply(axis=0)` returning per-column arrays, which silently failed to reshuffle row correspondence, producing a null median (0.81) as high as the real data and briefly suggesting the self factor was indistinguishable from noise. Both are recorded as failed attempts in NOTES.md rather than deleted. The number reported here is the third version, with the leakage removed and the null verified against known behaviour (pure noise should score .10-.35, matching the original 2026-07-31/08-16 characterisation) before being trusted.

datasheet.motivation: Characterise the phenomenology of 'pure awareness' / minimal phenomenal experience in meditators.
datasheet.composition: 3627 online submissions, 1403 in the analysis sample; 92 visual-analogue items 0-100 plus demographics, meditation history, tradition, religion, substance use, in 5 languages.
datasheet.collection: Self-selected online survey of meditators, Jan-Mar 2020.
datasheet.preprocessing: We impute item medians ONCE on the full analysis sample (never per subsample) so that every subgroup is scored on the same item set.
datasheet.caveats: Self-selected meditators reporting pure-awareness experiences specifically -- the deep/non-dual end of the state space, NOT the full range of practices. Language groups are very unbalanced (889/440/30/26/18). Meditation traditions are non-exclusive tick-boxes, not a partition.

relations.why: Self-reference marker: claims c3-c6 are ours, not the authors'. The authors make no replicability claim; we are not contradicting them on their own ground.

c3 qualifies c2 rather than refuting it. The 11/12/18 computation stands exactly as printed; what changes is its force. c2 says the count depends on the decision rule; c3 says that at half-sample resolution there is no discrete factor to count under any rule.
relations.asymmetric_note: Do not cite c3 as overturning c2. Anyone quoting '11 by parallel analysis' is quoting a correct number; they must also quote that none of those 11 reaches the criterion for being the same factor in two halves of one sample.

relations.why: Both literatures assume a stable underlying quantity that analysts merely estimate differently. Breznau shows analyst choices disperse the estimate; this record shows the estimand itself -- the factor structure -- is not stable across samples of the same population. The many-analysts programme measures dispersion around a target it never checks is there. Neither literature cites the other.

Same discipline of validating a dispersion instrument on synthetic data with a known answer before pointing it at real data -- the rule written after the estimator with algebraically zero power. Here it is validate_synthetic.py, and it is what licenses c3.
Same shape of result in a different field: variation between competent implementations of the same analysis is comparable to or larger than the reported uncertainty of any one of them.

c7 (this record) qualifies Lutz et al.'s claim that self-disidentification is purely a species of dereification. c7 shows the self/subject-object factor carries real, above-noise signal in a population selected for minimal discursive-thought content -- evidence against the strongest reductive reading (self-structure as pure epiphenomenon of thought-dereification) -- but c7 explicitly does NOT show exceptional stability, only ordinary stability, so it narrows rather than resolves the question. Do not cite this as refuting Lutz et al.; cite it as a data point their conceptual argument did not have.

open_questions: Does the clone deficit appear in other phenomenology questionnaires (MODTAS, PCI, 5D-ASC, MEQ30) with open raw data? If yes, this is a property of introspective self-report instruments and not of the MPE-92M. This is the single highest-value follow-up and it is directly runnable -- mpelib.py is instrument-agnostic given an item matrix.

If the heterogeneity is not along any recorded grouping, is it individual-level? A mixture model or a per-respondent stability index would test whether the population contains many small structures rather than two large ones.

Is the deficit an artifact of visual-analogue response styles (extreme vs midpoint responders) rather than of phenomenology? Testable by re-running the clone comparison after within-person standardisation of the 92 items.

What does the split-half congruence profile of a WELL-BEHAVED psychometric instrument look like at n=700 and 92 items? Without that reference the clone comparison is the only calibration, and one external benchmark would strengthen it a lot.
For CAT: report the split-half congruence of CAT's own dimensions. The expectation set by this record is that they will look like this. That must be planned for, not discovered at review.
